title: Is Your “Harmless” Drink Actually Fear in Disguise?
fullTitle: Soul Snack #89: Is Your “Harmless” Drink Actually Fear in Disguise?

promo.text: Learn how to connect with your intuition every day. Click here to start your journey to authentic power

description: At the heart of Gary’s response is the question of intention. Whether it is a drink at dinner, a smile across a room, or any habitual behavior, the real question is always the same: is this action coming from love or from fear?

Gary illustrates how what appears to be harmless social drinking can, upon closer examination, be a way of masking discomfort, seeking approval, or attempting to manipulate how others perceive you – all expressions of a frightened part of the personality.

The way forward is not judgment, but awareness. When life energy is used consciously and intentionally, with a genuine desire to contribute, connect, and create from love, even the smallest choices become opportunities to create authentic power .

chapters.title: Gary responds to the question of casual alcohol use by widening the lens:
chapters.text: rather than evaluating the behavior itself, he invites listeners to examine how they are using their life energy – and whether they are doing so consciously and intentionally.

chapters.title: Gary asks the essential question behind any behavior:
chapters.text: what is your intention? Is drinking – or any social habit – an attempt to mask feelings of fear, loosen up for approval, or influence how others feel about you? If so, that intention originates in fear, not in love.

chapters.title: Gary offers examples of what it looks like to redirect life energy toward love:
chapters.text: contributing to others, moving toward meaning and purpose, and choosing harmony, cooperation, and reverence for life over the need to please.

chapters.title: Gary shares that people in his programs have discovered their “casual” alcohol use was far less casual than they believed
chapters.text: and that the difficulty of giving it up revealed something important about the frightened parts of their personality that were active.

outro: Take out your notebook and think of a habit in your life that you have labeled “casual” or “harmless.” It doesn’t have to be alcohol – it could be anything you reach for when you feel uncomfortable, anxious, or unseen. Ask yourself honestly: what is my intention in this moment? Am I acting from love – from a genuine desire to contribute, connect, or create – or am I acting from fear? Write down what you notice, without judgment.
